description: The right-hand plot in Figure 7 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the CoLeG-R performance (measured as a percentage) of different LLaMA-2 model scales (7B, 13B, and 70B) when fine-tuned with varying sizes of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) datasets. The horizontal axis categorizes the models by size, while the vertical axis represents CoLeG-R (%) ranging from 0 to 80. For each model size, four bars are grouped together, corresponding to different SFT configurations as indicated in the legend: “no SFT” (light blue with diagonal stripes), “+ SFT on D₀” (orange with horizontal stripes), “+ SFT on D₀, D₁” (purple with diagonal stripes), and “+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂” (pink with diagonal stripes). The chart visually demonstrates that for all three model sizes, CoLeG-R scores increase as more datasets (D₀, then D₁, then D₂) are added to the SFT process. The 70B model consistently achieves the highest CoLeG-R scores across all SFT conditions, with the full dataset (D₀, D₁, D₂) yielding approximately 82%, while the 7B model’s best performance under the same condition is around 80%. The 13B model’s performance falls between the two, peaking at approximately 81% with the full dataset. The overall trend supports the caption’s claim that scaling up both model size and SFT dataset size improves CoLeG-R.
